title: Guava Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Guava Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Guava nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in bayabas, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Guava nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your bayabas (guava) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, zinc, magnesium and boron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Guava leaves with brown, scorched edges and small brown specks from potassium shortage

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc and boron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which guava nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a guava nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest guava nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in guava

Older leaves turn pale green to light yellow, usually starting at the tip, and in bad cases they die and drop. The tree grows slowly and stays small, with few new shoots, so it flowers and fruits less. You see it most at this stage: young trees, and bearing trees after heavy crops.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in bayabas
Trees that get little fertilizer, sandy soils low in organic matter, and heavy rain that washes nitrogen away.
How to tell it apart

Root knot and other nematodes also cause stunting, yellowing, wilting and dieback, as University of Florida notes. So check the roots for galls. To be sure, soil test and a leaf test of the third pair of leaves from the shoot tip. New growth that greens up after urea confirms it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

DA Caraga advises Complete 14 14 14 at 100 to 150 grams at planting and 200 to 300 grams per young tree. For bearing trees 300 grams to 1 kg of complete fertilizer plus 300 grams each of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 and 16 20 0, in a shallow furrow around the canopy edge, together with compost. India's National Horticulture Board gives 300 to 400 grams of nitrogen per bearing tree a year. For a quick lift, TNAU gives a Urea spray at 1 to 2 percent (10 to 20 grams per liter) every two weeks.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, fertilize every year in splits during the rains and add compost or manure under the canopy.
Phosphorus deficiency in guava

Growth is slow, weak and stunted. Older leaves turn dark or blue green, and in bad cases leaves and stems take a purple color. Fruit matures late and develops poorly. In India this shows as leaf bronzing: purple to red specks scattered over the leaves, a bronze or copper color on older leaves, heavy leaf fall in bad cases. Brown patterns on the fruit skin. You see it most at this stage: young trees, and bearing trees once fruiting begins, when the tree pulls nutrients from old leaves into the fruit.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in bayabas
Poor, acid soils. In bronzed guava orchards in India, soils were low in fertility and pH.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also gives bronze or reddish patches between the veins of old leaves, but the veins stay clearly green. Potassium deficiency scorches the leaf edges. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH. A leaf test of the third pair of leaves from the shoot tip for nitrogen, phosphorus, potash and zinc together.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

In an Indian study, bronzing was largely overcome by spraying 0.5 percent DAP (Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0, 5 grams per liter) together with Zinc sulfate every week for two months. TNAU gives DAP at 2 percent every two weeks. For the soil, DA Caraga gives bearing trees 300 grams of 16 20 0 plus complete fertilizer and potash. Lime very acid soils, following the soil test.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a complete fertilizer with phosphorus and potash every year from the time trees start to bear, plus compost, and correct acid soils.
Potassium deficiency in guava

blocks.alt: Guava leaves with brown, scorched edges and small brown specks from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson, CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: The edges of older leaves turn yellow and then scorch brown. Growth is slow, stems are weak, and fruits stay smaller and fewer. Shortage of potash, with phosphorus, is also linked to leaf bronzing once trees start to fruit. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, during fruit growth.
Why potassium deficiency happens in bayabas
Sandy and leached soils, heavy crops, and programs that give nitrogen only. Indian course notes tie bronzing to soils marginal in phosphorus and potash.
How to tell it apart

Phosphorus shortage and bronzing give purple to red specks over the leaf rather than a scorched edge. Salt damage also browns leaf tips and edges, with leaf drop and dieback, as University of Florida notes. To be sure, soil test for potash and a leaf test of the third pair of leaves from the shoot tip.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

DA Caraga gives bearing trees 300 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 with complete fertilizer and 16 20 0. India's National Horticulture Board gives 250 to 350 grams of K2O per bearing tree a year. Notes that Sulfate of potash sprays at 1 to 2 percent raised yield and fruit quality. TNAU gives a 2 percent spray every two weeks.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, raise the potash share once trees bear.
Zinc deficiency in guava

The youngest leaves come out small, narrow and pointed, with raised veins. The blade cups up or down along the midrib, with the edges turned in. Leaves yellow strongly between the veins while the veins stay bright green, and small brown dots spread over the blade. Shoots stay thin and the tree stays dwarfed. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, and orchards on poor soils where bronzing also shows.
Why zinc deficiency happens in bayabas
High pH soils, heavy phosphate fertilizer, and poor, acid soils low in zinc and organic matter, where bronzed Indian orchards had low leaf zinc.
How to tell it apart

Iron deficiency also keeps green veins on yellow young leaves. But the leaves keep a normal shape, turn fully yellow and then whitish, and lower leaves stay normal. To be sure, leaf test of the third pair of leaves from the shoot tip. In a Brazilian trial deficient seedlings held 9 ppm zinc against 14 ppm in healthy ones.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Spray Zinc sulfate with DAP every week for two months, as the Indian bronzing study did (DAP at 0.5 percent). Indian guides also give a spray of 0.3 percent Zinc sulfate (3 grams per liter) with 0.4 percent boric acid before flowering, which raised yield and fruit size. Course notes give 100 grams of Zinc sulfate per tree to the soil on bronzed trees.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid heavy phosphate and overliming, add compost, and include zinc in a pre flowering spray where leaf tests run low.
Magnesium deficiency in guava

Older leaves develop yellow, bronze or reddish patches between the veins while the veins stay green. In bad cases younger leaves show it too and leaves fall early. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, mostly on acid soils.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in bayabas
Acid soils, and heavy potash or calcium fertilizer, which compete with magnesium.
How to tell it apart

Bronzing from low phosphorus and zinc also gives purple to red specks on the leaves. A leaf test tells them apart. To be sure, leaf test of the third pair of leaves from the shoot tip, and a soil test for magnesium, potash and calcium together.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

TNAU gives a foliar spray of Magnesium sulfate at 2 percent (20 grams per liter) every two weeks. On acid soils use Dolomite, following the soil test. University of Florida advises 4 to 6 percent magnesium in the mix for young trees.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils with Dolomite and keep potash and magnesium in balance.
Boron deficiency in guava

The youngest leaves come out narrower than normal, pale, with a dark net of veins on a light background. They thicken, turn brittle and curl or twist downward as if the leaf stalk were broken. The top pairs drop while older leaves stay. Later the growing points die and branches dry from the tip down. You see it most at this stage: new flushes and before flowering.
Why boron deficiency happens in bayabas
No guava particular soil causes were found in the sources. The Brazilian trial notes that boron interacts with calcium and phosphorus in the leaf.
How to tell it apart

Aphids feeding on young growth also curl the leaves, as DA Caraga notes. But you can see the insects and the leaves are not thick and brittle. To be sure, leaf test of the third pair of leaves from the shoot tip. In the Brazilian trial deficient seedlings held 7 ppm boron against 43 ppm in healthy ones.
What to apply for boron deficiency

TNAU gives a foliar spray of Borax at 0.5 percent every two weeks. Indian guides also give boric acid at 0.4 percent with zinc sulfate before flowering. Boron is toxic in excess, so do not repeat high doses without a test.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add organic matter and include a small boron dose in a pre flowering spray where tests run low.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any guava nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your bayabas needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Guava nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my bayabas leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: old leaves pale green to light yellow from the tip. Slow, thin tree with few fruits. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in guava?
items.a: DA Caraga advises Complete 14 14 14 at 100 to 150 grams at planting and 200 to 300 grams per young tree. For bearing trees 300 grams to 1 kg of complete fertilizer plus 300 grams each of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 and 16 20 0, in a shallow furrow around the canopy edge, together with compost.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in guava?
items.a: In an Indian study, bronzing was largely overcome by spraying 0.5 percent DAP (Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0, 5 grams per liter) together with Zinc sulfate every week for two months. TNAU gives DAP at 2 percent every two weeks.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in guava?
items.a: DA Caraga gives bearing trees 300 grams of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 with complete fertilizer and 16 20 0. India's National Horticulture Board gives 250 to 350 grams of K2O per bearing tree a year.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my bayabas lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the guava nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
